utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number, IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: General Talic, good afternoon to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TALIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Yes, I can hear in a language I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Brdjanin, can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Yes, I can hear you and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Joanna Korner, Andrew Cayley, Denise Gustin, case manager, for the Prosecution. Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Ms. Korner. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm John Ackerman, I'm here with Milan Trbojevic, my co-counsel, and Marela Jevtovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Appearances for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. My name is Slobodan Zecevic, and Ms. Natasha Ivanovic-Fauveau. We will represent Mr. Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you Mr. Zecevic. Welcome to this Tribunal. As you know, we started the Trial in late January. There's quite a bit to catch up with, but I've heard very good references about you and I'm sure that you will give a very valid contribution which we very much look forward to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We certainly are going to do to the best of our abilities, my dear colleague Ms. Fauveau and myself. However, you do understand that I feel like I am boarding the boat and left the luggage in the port of embarkment. But anyhow, please be assured that we will do our best in representing our client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I did that once when sailing to Sicily. It was no problem. When I got to Sicily, I got everything from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour but this appears to be a around the world trip. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And I can also assure you, Mr. Zecevic, that Madam Fauveau has been following this case sedulously from the very -- the word go and that she has done a very good job and she has cooperated fully with this Tribunal. So she should be in a position to put you in the picture without great difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: By all means, Your Honours. If that wasn't the case, I would have never accepted the appointment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So witness, good afternoon to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome back. We will be continuing with your evidence, testimony. And before we do so, the usher will hand to you the copy -- the text of the solemn declaration which I would like you to repeat. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour knows the difficulties I have today, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Space, first and foremost.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, apart from space. But also I'm in the middle of calling a witness in Judge Schomburg's court. There are a number of administrative matters to deal with but Mr. Cayley is going to deal with them at a later stage. I think it would be worth leaving something like 20 minutes at the end of the session to deal with them all. Your Honours, may I just mention this, that with Your Honours' agreement, because of the difficulties, if I may leave the minute I've finished and Mr. Cayley will cover for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Please yourself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, one of the administrative matters would have been that over the intervening week we've had an investigator go to Sanski Most and take photographs amongst other things of the interior of, first of all, the police station cells and then of the garages, Betonirka. Your Honour, the Defence only arrived a few minutes ago, so I don't know whether they've been given copies -- they have, but just now. Unless there is objection, however, I would like to show Mr. Zulic the -- some of the photographs that were taken. And Your Honours, we haven't at the moment got sufficient copies, but I'll put them up on the ELMO and we will have copies tomorrow for Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Thank you. Incidentally, Ms. Korner -- the Prosecution requests 20 minutes' time for some administrative points to be raised. Is there anything that the Defence would like to raise either now or later, any preliminaries? If we could leave them for later towards the end of the sitting -- of the sitting, it will be better, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think there are some things we want to discuss. But later is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is fine with us as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So just let me know, Mr. Ackerman, Mr. Zecevic, how much time you require. We have 20 minutes from the -- for the Prosecution and if you require some time, let me know. Another ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, when I said 20 minutes, that was including the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It won't take us 20 minutes to deal with the matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Ms. Korner. With regard to the photos.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can we go ahead, Mr. Ackerman, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Your Honours, I was just looking at if photographs, but I believe there -- we don't have any problem with going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We can go forward, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Zulic, welcome back, if that's the right word. Can you just remind us again. When you were taken to the garages and held as a prisoner, which garage were you kept in?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In garage number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'd like you to have a look, please, at some photographs. And first of all, can you have a look at one that's been marked with the number 0124-9107. And if that could be placed on the ELMO as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that, Mr. Zulic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is the police station. But something seems to be lacking there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's leave that one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I have that one back. Your Honour will appreciate I never had a chance to show these to -- okay. Could you look -- can I have that one back, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And could you have a look, please, at 0124-9114.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the garages.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you just indicate by using the pointer which you're calling the third garage.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- doesn't look the same as it used to. But as you enter this way and the entrance is here, so the third garage would be this one, at the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. I'm sorry. Did you say you were held in the third garage or the first garage?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first. In the first.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Just to avoid any possible confusion. Mr. Zulic, could you point again, once more, to the garage in which you were kept, which you are now saying was garage number 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that it was this one. This was the first garage.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Just for the record, the witness points at the garage which is at the extreme right of the photo, being the first one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's right. Your Honours, I'm going to ask that the photographs all become a joint exhibit number, A, B, C, D, and the like or 1, 2, and 3. So if that could be made Prosecutor's Exhibit 824.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Will you take note of that, Madam Registrar, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to have a look please, at a photograph of the inside of garage number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, which bears the number 0124-9113. Your Honour, there's a statement from the investigator showing which the garages are.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Zulic, did the garage look like that when you were kept inside it?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The door wasn't there, this door.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one that can be seen here. That wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But otherwise, it was more or less like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, could that be made 824.2.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just remind us. How many people were kept in there, Mr. Zulic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In one garage there were up to 30 people, 30 men.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'm just checking the numbers. I just want to make sure -- right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then could you have a look, please, at this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the same cell. It's 0124-9121, or the same building, in which you can see the window to the left-hand side of it as one looks at it. The witness, Mr. Karabeg, went with the investigator and sat down just to show the -- the space.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: First of all, is -- was that window like that when you were in it, Mr. Zulic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What was the difference?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the window there was a -- a pallet of concrete blocks which was about 10 centimetres away from the frame, so that it didn't look quite like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When the -- this building had 30 people in it, were you able to sit down in the position that we can see Mr. Karabeg in?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most frequently there wasn't enough room.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, you can take that. Your Honour, could that be made 3 -- 824.3. Thank you. And there's one further photograph. Yes. Thank you very much. And that's 0124-9123.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that's just taken from the outside looking into the same block. Were those corrugated iron doors the same, Mr. Zulic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Only I apologise. What we were looking at was garage number 3, not number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh. You're quite right.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first picture. So I apologise. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. You were in 3. You're quite right. In which case I ought really to -- because the window is the other side.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's my fault. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I show you 0124-9116. Is that -- was the window that side as you look at it?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then Your Honour, I'm sorry, I ought to withdraw the other two -- the one I showed with Mr. Karabeg and the other one. It should be -- so this one will become -- yes. If I withdraw the one that's .3 and make this one .3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just substitute.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Substitute the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have them substituted. And they have not yet been admitted formally as exhibits anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So it's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I won't bother about the last one -- no. Yes. That's the right one. 113 is right. That is -- oh, no. That's cell number 1. I'm sorry, Your Honour. I do apologise. I'm afraid it's been a bit chaotic. I ought to withdraw all -- 113, the photograph of the inside as well, so that this photograph will become 0124-9116 and that will become Prosecutor's Exhibit 824.2. So just two photographs. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that too much of a problem?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We'll sort it out at the break just to make sure that this time we've got it right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I'm totally confused, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're not the only one, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to sort it out. But one -- the two that I'm asking now to be exhibited are the one that has the number 0124-9114 and 0124-9116, two photographs only, outside and inside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As I understand it, it's the first of this series of photos which we saw there were -- there were the three garages; correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And those are 824.1 and 824.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You're changing .3 to 2 now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly. There are only two and not three photos.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Zulic, I now want to go back to what happened to you. You described to us at the end of last week -- the week before, rather, the beatings and what happened inside Betonirka. And I think it's right that you've described in detail virtually on a daily basis what happened to you and the other people who were being held in Betonirka in the diary that you made up, compiled at the end of 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And is it right also that you have a full description of virtually everything that happened on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have perhaps 10 per cent because this was what I could remember, what I was able to think over and recollect. I probably didn't write down everything. I may even have made a mistake. But I hope no one will take it against me. And if I did insult anyone or I mentioned a name by mistake. But I mostly wrote down the things that I was able to write down at that moment, things that I remembered, because I'm not accustomed to writing, so I just wanted to take note of what I remembered.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And have you got with you today, should anybody want to look at them, the three -- original three exercise books? Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you though, about a particular incident that you described in your diary. On the 22nd of June, were you taken out of the garage?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is page 10 of the statement. And in the diary it's page 6 of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you taken out of the garage and taken --

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- in Mercedes car to an area --

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the vehicle was a Mercedes, owned by Ilham Oric [phoen] before the war. This vehicle was seized and they drove it. And they took me to Kriva Cesta.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, is that an area which is close to the Partisan cemetery?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is about 700 metres from the Partisan cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'd like you to take the map, please, of Sanski Most, the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do now have the ones with photographs but with no subtitling. So I'm going to ask that that be shown to the witness. This is a version of P757.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we see the Partisan cemetery marked on that map? Do you have your spectacles with you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise for a moment. I'm looking for my glasses. No, that is not it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This Partizansko groblje is in Kruhari -- Partisan cemetery in Kruhari.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see Kriva Cesta here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. How far away is Kriva Cesta?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kriva Cesta is about 2 kilometres away from Betonirka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction of Caplje.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Could you have a look, please, at -- if you take that map back and if you have a look, please, at another map. You'll see that Caplje has been marked on it. And if you could just have a look at that and indicate to us where --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Does this have an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: For the record, I think we ought to indicate what it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, we will when I get the map back and I discover what the exhibit number is, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Looking at that, you'll see that Caplje is marked. Whereabouts is Kriva Cesta, roughly?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kriva Cesta is here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And there's a Partisan cemetery there, is there?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 700 metres down the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly 700 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And is that area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Ms. Korner. For the record, the witness is pointing to a spot right above the place where Zegar is indicated on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And just before we take the map away and I give Mr. Ackerman the exhibit number --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is there a sort of river there or a stream of some sort?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just below the road, about 5 metres below, there's a stream. The road is above the stream.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And at a large bend in the road, it passes under -- under it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. If you could let me have the map back. Thank you very much, Mr. Zulic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the exhibit number is 757 -- P757.3.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you were taken there. And were you taken there by the same people who had arrested you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you just tell us what their names are again.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Macura Gojko, Mahunic, but I have to look it up in my notebook. Unfortunately I've forgotten his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. If I put the names to you, perhaps you can agree with them, as you say you've listed in your notebook. Was there somebody called Predrag Maric?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Peda. Maybe it's been misinterpreted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Somebody called Macura?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Macura, Gojko. Gojko is his first name. Mahuna.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mahuna?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mahuna, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was --

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had a scar here on his cheek.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And finally was there somebody called Dosenovic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was. Dosenovic. He's a driver. Peda or Predrag, he was the third policeman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, when you got to the area, what happened?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something happened before we arrived. There were men there already, the army, soldiers. So that I arrived one but last, actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The men who were there, the soldiers, what sort of uniform did they have on?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They wore olive-grey uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And could you tell which unit they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really am unable to tell which unit they belonged to, whether they were Chetniks or the regular army, regular troops, because they were behind some willow trees, so that we just saw some soldiers. I couldn't see them properly. But I saw a second group of men that were sitting down about 20 metres away from the stream. What was -- what were they sitting? Was there a table, or were they just sitting by the side of the tree -- by the side of the -- near the stream? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a table but not next to the stream but about 20 or 20 metres away from the stream -- 25 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of those people who were sitting at the table?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognised Nedeljko Rasula. He was sitting in civilian clothes. He had a white coat on, not absolutely white but with some colours on it, with sort of dark -- a dark pattern on a white background. And I recognised Milan Raus, he went to school with me for some 12 years. I recognised Nemanja Tripkovic. I recognised the two Senic brothers. They're both Montenegrins. One used to work with me in the mine and the other was a teacher of art in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Anybody else?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But just now I can't remember any more names.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Was anybody -- you say that Rasula was wearing a white coat with some colours on it. Can you remember what the others were wearing? Was anybody in uniform?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nemanja Tripkovic had a camouflage uniform on. Milan Raus was wearing an olive-grey uniform. But I think it was an officer's uniform, not the ordinary soldier's uniform. The two Senic brothers were also in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Did you make a list of those men that you recognised in your diary?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm a million per cent sure about these, but as for others I did my best as far as I could. I didn't want to hurt anyone. But as best I could remember I noted down all the people that I recognised because there were a lot of people among them that used to work with me before the war and that we even visited one another. We were on good terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, perhaps if you can find the part of your diary. It's on our page 8 in the translation -- where you -- you had something -- it started day 4, and then you gave a list of the people that you recognised sitting at this table. And I'm just going to ask you to confirm without reading out all the names that that was the list. It's in the first book of your diary, Mr. Zulic, very close to the end.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, the first book. I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You listed Rasula then Vlado Vrkes. Was he one that you're sure was there?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vlado Vrkes, Drago Delic -- yes. He was there. Not his sons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was Tomo Delic there?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And a number of others. And the other only one I want to ask you about, did you also see there someone who you later remembered to be a general of the former JNA, now retired, called Daljevic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assumed that it was him. I didn't recognise him. But as far as I could remember -- because in our head office in the autumn of 1991 - I don't know the exact date - but coal was being sold at the time and I sat with him and we talked and I assume that it was him. But I can't claim 1.000 per cent, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But as -- in respect of Rasula, Vrkes, the Delics, and the other people you've mentioned, are you sure that they were there?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regarding Rasula, 1.000 per cent. Vrkes and Nemanja, Tomo and Drago Delic, I know those people. And as soon as they start speaking, I can recognise their voices. I don't even have to turn around. Maybe today I wouldn't be able to recognise them at all. But if they were to speak, I would recognise them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedeljko Rasula was a teacher for eight years, and Nemanja Tripkovic I used to work for him in his home. I know Drago and Tomo Delic very well, because they are from Krkojevci.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are stone cutters.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's fine. Now, can you tell us having -- you saw these men there. You saw that there were already people wearing military uniform when you arrived at the spot. Were there other people there as well outside the military?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were men there who did the digging. And when I was taken out, I was given a shovel as well -- a hoe, and I was taken to the stream and told to dig.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you were taken out of the car, given a hoe, and made to dig. How many other people were there who were also having to dig?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were approximately 20 to 22 men.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of those men?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognised Ibro Eminic next to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And anyone else?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lolo or Smail Pasic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was everyone having to dig?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you told what you were digging?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who ordered you to dig?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally was ordered by Macura.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At that stage, whilst you were digging, what did you believe that you were digging?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, actually I did have an anticipation of what I was digging.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what was that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I supposed I was digging a grave for myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you stop digging?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We continued digging but it was very difficult to dig out anything in that stream.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And so how did the digging come to an end?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these men were slaughtered. Their throats were cut. And I was the only one to survive, together with two other men that were brought in from another place [As translated]. Their names were Ceric and Halkic. They were returned, brought back.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You say their throats were cut. Who cut --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise Mr. Ackerman. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm told that he said two other men that were brought from Zdena, from not another place, as the transcript says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zulic, the other two persons that survived together with you, you said something, that they had been brought from some place. Where had they come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zdena. I think that it is also in my diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Zulic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I -- you said, Mr. Zulic, their throats were cut. Who cut their throats?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simo Simetic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did he cut all -- you said there were about 20 to 22 men and three survived. Did he cut all their throats?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did. I think he did. But I couldn't look a lot. I had to -- from the place where I was down there. I only heard the screams. I saw Ibro Eminic when his throat was cut. He stabbed a knife right here, on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were there members of the -- the military people that you saw, were they standing round?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They stood with their rifles pointed at them. And as soon as somebody got up, they would shoot. One -- we would hear a shot. I know that Ibro was found, Ibro Eminic, on the Sana bank. And there are no traces of others.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just so that we understand, these people were standing there, the military were pointing guns at them, and this man was going around cutting people's throats.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably it had to be that way, because they were telling him, "Simo, slow down. You're working too fast." Simo was not a mentally healthy person, even before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who was saying, "Simo slow down. You're working too fast"?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these people from the group were saying that, those people that sat at the table.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you hear Rasula saying anything?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would recognise his voice any time, because when Simo got to me he said, "Simo, leave him alone."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did anybody else from that table that was watching say anything?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they cursed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did the men at the table have anything to drink with them?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did anybody say anything to Simo while this was happening in respect of drink?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were saying, "Simo, have a drink. You'll work better after that. When one has a drink, one works better after that."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The men who were being slaughtered, were they all of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. From what I could hear from Ibro, they -- I don't know. I can't claim that they were all Muslims. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did anybody at the table at that stage while the killing was happening say anything about Muslims? And what was that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were calling us balija, you know, using those kind of terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm afraid the interpreter missed his answer. He did say "yes," and I heard him, but it doesn't show up on the -- on the screen. What happened -- you say that Rasula said that you should be left alone. What happened to you though?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when Rasula said that, then Macura said, "We'll send you back. We'll take you back as well." And then he said, "Open your mouth," and he put a pistol into my mouth. And Mahuna put a pistol to my right side and said, "Shall we change his religion now? Shall we make a cross on him now?" And Macura say, "We need him alive." And they pulled the trigger and I thought I'd been killed. But he pulled the pistol out and knocked out these two teeth. Then they kicked me into my back, and I was about to fall into the stream and then they took me back to the police station -- or rather, to Betonirka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I just want to make sure we all understand. One man had the pistol to your head, and one man had a pistol in your mouth. Who pulled the trigger? Which man? The one with the pistol to your head?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did it fire?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did. And I thought at that moment that I was dead. However, when I came to, after that fear, I realised that nothing had happened to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The one who had the pistol in your mouth, you say that he knocked two -- two of your front teeth out. What -- as he pulled the pistol out?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you say you were then taken back to Betonirka. Did --

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Other than Rasula saying that you shouldn't be killed, what was the attitude of Rasula and his companions to this killing?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that -- I can't describe their attitude there, but I believe that they were laughing, as I could see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: One final matter on this incident. You say that after the throat-cutting, people were shot. Were that people who tried to get away or who hadn't been killed instantly?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on what I could see with Ibro, those that didn't die instantly, on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As far as you could see, did anybody try and run away?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I couldn't see that. And I don't think that they were able to run away.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you were only able to see the person closest to you, were you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the person closest to me, because they didn't let us turn to the side. So what I was able to see I saw from Cesta, from the road. And we were not allowed to turn to the side. And Ibro stood, well, less than 50 centimetres away from me, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think you drew for the investigator a plan. I'd like you to have a look, please, at that. It was attached to the statement. I haven't got a copy of it there. I can't find mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's -- the original B/C/S version which the witness drew and also an English version, which we handed in. I think there's one on -- if Your Honours have found it. It's marked with his initials -- it's got the ERN number 02061819 on it. And we may want to put it up on the ELMO. We could put the English on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. You've indicated there -- perhaps we could just have a look at the top of it. At the top right-hand side, where we see next to "Partisan cemetery", is that -- you're pointing at the car, are you? I mean, you've drawn the car plus the four men.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have three men here, and this -- down here are soldiers. I drew where the soldiers stood, several soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Could you use the pointer and just point at the ELMO. That's the car.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Soldiers.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then where you've marked it with an "X" are those the people who were shot -- who were killed? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the table is where you've marked it, is it? That Rasula and people were sitting at.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry. That's my fault. Is what you're pointing at now where you say the table was?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what --

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the path down was right here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us, please, where you've got from -- you've got an arrow pointing towards the table with two little circles there. What's that meant to indicate?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two circles indicate where -- the place where the remains of Partisan used to be, from the Second World War. So these were Partisan graves.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And so -- but where you've written "Rasula" and "Davidovic," they're just two of the people who were at the table; is that right? It's not that they're -- you're indicating that they were closer --

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is how I drew this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understand that. But are you -- are you saying that Rasula and Davidovic were actually at the table? They weren't as close as where you've written their names.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were at the table.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And down there you've written the names of three -- the three men who brought you there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may that be made Prosecutor's Exhibit 825, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Davidovic, do you know what he did?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that before the war he was a police commander and he was a member of the presidency of the municipality and he had a rank of reserve captain, and I know that he was head of a unit. I think it was called -- of the 6th Krajina unit -- Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. So you survived, and you were taken back to Betonirka.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think you told us that only one body out of the other people that were killed has been recovered.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So far only one body has been recovered, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you, then next, about your transfer to Manjaca. On the 7th of July were you taken to Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you describe that incident in your diary?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Using your diary if necessary to help you remember, can you tell us what happened during that trip to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before they boarded us, they beat us first. All of us were taken out two by two to the room in the administrative building, and we were taken then there two by two. And since that place had a total of three rooms, this is where they took us two by two. Then they took us back and boarded on a truck. It was a -- a regular truck with a passenger cabin in front.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you say they took you two by two to the administrative building. Was that in the police station?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was right behind Betonirka, about 15 metres from Betonirka. This is where they normally took us to beat us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, it may be that it will help to -- maybe not. No. All right. I'm not sure we've got a photograph of that. What was the weather like that day?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was extremely hot that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you were placed onto this -- they boarded you onto a truck. How many people got into that truck?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know the exact number until we were told that there were 64 of us, because we didn't know how many people were in garage number 2 and 3 and we had no possibility of seeing the other people. The only way of communication in the garage was knocking on the wall.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So they said that there were 64 of you. How many people on that truck did you know?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out of those people, I knew more than half. I knew more than half of them. However, I didn't know that they were there. Because, for example, when we went out to lunch, only the people out of garage number 1 would go. And then after we had our lunch very quickly, we would go back to the garage and then they would take people out of garage number 2. So it was very difficult to communicate and to know who were the other people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understand that. But once you were on the truck, did you realise that you knew more than half.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did that include Enver Burnic?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Burnic, Enver. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what about someone called Haso Osmancevic? Was he on the truck as well?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was taken to the police station on that day that morning. He was with me in the garage number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you told us that they beat you at the administration building before you were put on the truck. When you were put on the truck, did they beat you?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Once they boarded us onto the truck, they pulled the canvas tarpaulin and locked the truck. I don't know how to explain. They simply locked it. They pulled the ropes that held the canvas tarpaulin so it wouldn't flutter in the back. So they simply pulled it together and locked us in and they did that before as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the people who put you onto the truck, were they policemen or military or civilians?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brane Sobot was the only one who wore civilian clothes. And the rest of them were policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Once you were all on the truck and the tarpaulin had been secured, did the truck set off?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it set off.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did it go on its journey to Manjaca without stopping, or did it stop?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It stopped twice; once for a very brief time, and the second time it seemed like an eternity because we had no more water.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Had they given you water when you set off?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But some people managed to grab some water or were given water from the guards, and then they managed to take it with them. That was all we had. For instance, if we got water yesterday, then that was what was left for us to drink and for treatment of wounds. These were 2-litre jerrycans roughly, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the jerrycans were at Betonirka, not on the truck. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who managed -- as they were boarding us onto the truck with batons, they were forcing us to climb on. And if somebody managed to take a jerrycan with him, they did. But as far as I know, only three such jerrycans of water were taken onto the truck. So that would be roughly about 6 litres of water.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I was going to ask how big that was. So you ran out of water. Did anybody try and get hold of water by attracting the attention of the guards?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No. He didn't try to get water but air. But a woman wanted to give us some water. I don't know who that woman was, because we were crying out of the truck and asking for water, and then the guards were cursing and shooting and telling her not to give us water. Who that woman was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So was she allowed to give you water?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What was the atmosphere like on the truck? How much air was there by this stage?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How much air there was? It's hard to describe. I know that it was lacking, because the sun was burning through the tarpaulin, so that we were short of air. And I learnt when we reached the Vrhpolje Bridge - there was a checkpoint there - and we heard a conversation. The truck stopped for a while, and there was a conversation between the policemen and the people at the checkpoint at the Vrhpolje Bridge, and they were cursing and saying, "Give us those balijas. Where are you taking them through, Vrhpolje?" And it is from that that I knew that we were at Vrhpolje. And by then already on my lap a boy had died.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the boy?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, but just now I can't remember. If I may try and collect myself for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, one moment. Mr. Zulic, if you need a break, you can have a break. Do you -- would you like us to stop now for some time? Yes. The sitting is suspended for 30 minutes, resuming 30 minutes from now. Is -- am I causing you trouble, Ms. Korner? Because I realise that I am causing you a problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I appreciate with the -- would it possible to say 20 minutes, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have any difficulties? 20 minutes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we need a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I fully appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Zulic, I know this is distressing for you, but if we can just finish what happened on the truck. You've told us about the boy that died on your lap. Did other people die during the course of that journey that you realised had died?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw people dying. A couple of times his head would nod. He would foam at the mouth and then he would die. The worst death that we witnessed -- there were two brothers, Nedzad and Rane Muhic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Why was -- I'm sorry to ask you, but why was that the worst?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They hugged each other, and they cried out, "Don't let me die, brother. It's too early for me to die. We won't die."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you know how old they were roughly?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly 30 to 35, 36 maybe.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you or anyone else in the truck drink anything other than water to try and quench your thirst?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had on me a small bottle of shaving lotion called Brioni [phoen]. I drank that first, and they told me not to drink that because it wouldn't help. After that, when I sort of came to again, I urinated into the bottle and then I drank it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Manjaca, who took you out of the truck?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody removed the canvas and said, "Balija, come out, you motherfuckers. What are you waiting for?" But I apologise. First they started calling out names, and then they started saying, "Come out, you balijas. What are you waiting for?" So I got the order wrong for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's all right. The men who had died, how were they taken out of the truck?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't take them out of the truck. They carried out six men who were neither alive nor dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What, who were unconscious?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who carried the men out? Was it the men who had escorted you to Manjaca, or was it men who were at the camp? Did you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These people from the truck who were still able to walk, they did it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you got out of the truck -- outside the truck, did you recognise any of the guards who were there?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just at that moment when I got off, no. But later on I recognised them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who was present that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brane Sobot.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The men who had taken you -- arrested you and taken you to the river, Dosenovic, Mahunic, Macura, were they there?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they escorted the convoy. They were in Betonirka and they escorted the convoy. They boarded us at Betonirka into the trucks and they escorted the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you say that the unconscious men were taken out of the truck. They were six. Were you the only person -- were you one of the people carried out, or were you able to get out on your own?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got out with the help of Enver Burnic and Bekir.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And? I'm sorry. I didn't catch the last person.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Enver Burnic and Bekir Delic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. What happened then to the men who had died?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They called Dr. Sabanovic first, a detainee, and he examined those who were half dead and he said they couldn't be saved without proper medical care. And just then - I didn't know who it was - but an officer said that all the shit should be boarded onto the bus so that they didn't -- wouldn't stink and that they should be taken back to Sana. He didn't want any dead people in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you find out later who that officer was who said that the shit should be boarded onto the bus?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Bozidar Popovic or Pavlovic. But I think it was Popovic. He had an accent, a Montenegrin accent.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was he -- did you later discover he was the person who was in charge of Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What about the men who were unconscious and Mr. Burnic? What happened to him -- or what happened to them, first of all, the unconscious men?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Burnic was not unconscious. He was taken back. So was Biscevic and Mauzner and another young man whom I really don't know. They were taken back in good health. They were asked to load these unconscious men and then to unload them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Load -- sorry. Load them where and unload them from where?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was said -- this lieutenant colonel said that they should be loaded and Brane Sobot said Bekir was chosen to go together with Biscevic, Mauzner, and another man I didn't know. But -- let them load them onto the vehicle and let them unload them at Sana.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So was this the situation, that the dead men and the unconscious men were both taken away? Both -- all of them were taken away?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How many men from that truck entered Manjaca that evening? There was yourself and how many others?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Betonirka -- according to what I know, there were about 30 of us who got on, or 36 -- I'm sorry, 36 or 38 of us. I learnt that later, actually; not at the time, but I learnt it later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Zulic, I'm sorry. It's my fault. I meant to ask you this: After the dead men and the unconscious men were separated out, how many of you actually physically went into the camp from that truck?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not alone from Betonirka. There were people from the sports hall who had been brought there at that time. So I don't know what you mean. Just from Betonirka or from the sports hall as well, in total?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. What I mean is from that truck -- and you said there was something like 64 men on it -- how many survived and were physically able to go into Manjaca camp and become a prisoner in Manjaca camp?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that between 36 and 38 men that I could remember afterwards -- it was established later, actually, with precision that only about half, 34 men, entered Manjaca, when we counted. This is according to my calculations.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. You say that Dr. Sabanovic came and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours. But the part of the translation didn't get into the -- into the transcript. If this can be clarified by my learned colleague, because the witness has said that only 34 or -- 34 people from Betonirka came into Manjaca, and it appears that the other -- the other prisoners were taken from somewhere else. That is why I think it's irrelevant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's clarify this, Mr. Zulic. How many -- on the truck, how many were from Betonirka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the truck? That entered the camp, 34 people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Dead or alive.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 34 people from Betonirka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And from the other --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 64. 64.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 64 in all from Betonirka and from the other place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Only from Betonirka there were 64 men. From other places, from the sports hall, there were about 700 to 800 men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. But -- on the day -- we are interested only on the same -- what happened on the day when you arrived in Manjaca. You arrived in a particular truck. How many persons were carried on that truck? How many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said that on the truck there were 64. But there wasn't just one truck. That's what I was saying. I mentioned the people from the sports hall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But on that truck on which you were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 64.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From Betonirka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And they were all from Betonirka? In your truck, were you all from Betonirka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And out of those 64, how many were then admitted to Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to my calculations, 34.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think it was that unclear. I thought there was a complaint about the translation. I think we've just gone round the houses now. I think he's made it quite clear there were 64 people on the truck, 34 entered Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What wasn't clear was whether they were all from Betonirka or whether they were also from the sports -- that was quite unclear even in my mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But now it's clear enough. I mean, we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Zulic, Dr. Sabanovic, the doctor you said who was called, had you met him before? Did you know him before you arrived at Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you quite briefly about Manjaca, Mr. Zulic, because again I think in your diary you wrote a fairly full, even if not everything that happened, description of what happened in the camp. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, yes, though many things have been left out. But I haven't -- I didn't memorise everything when I was writing it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I understand that. But everybody has the diary and so we can look at it. I just want, as it were, to deal with certain topics, themes of what life in Manjaca was like. First of all, can you tell us which stable you were put into.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were first taken to stable number 6, and three days later we were transferred to stable number 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And when you got to the stable, what happened if you had to use the toilet?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First ten men had to line up, form a line, and then all of them had to go to the toilet, whether they needed to or not, whether only one or two wanted to go. You couldn't go where you wanted; for instance, you were not allowed to trample on Serb grass.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did anything happen to the property belonging to the people who were going to the toilet in groups of ten?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If they were to see a good pair of tennis shoes, Puma tennis shoes or a leather jacket, this would be taken away and another pair of shoes would be given to him, regardless of the size. Or if they take off the jacket, they would give them a soldier's shirt to wear.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did any of the prisoners have personal property left, watches or jewellery, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were people who came from Betonirka with us that day -- no, I'm sorry, from the sports hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And they had -- they still had personal possessions left, did they?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had all their documents on them because they were detained in the sports hall in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What happened to their property, things like watches, identification papers, and the like?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would enter the stable and order us to turn around and face the wall. And then we had to put our hands on our backs - that was the command - heads down, and if they would see a good watch on someone's hand, they would simply take it. And they started some sort of medical examination, and there was a Dr. Meho Derviskadic and a Serbian nurse, male nurse or doctor - I don't know what he was - he was sitting at a table, and he would write things down, and we had to strip for the examination and two policemen would search through personal belongings, seize valuables, and separate documents to one side and the objects found on the detainees on another, like watches, rings, chains, money.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The policemen, by this stage was it policemen from Sanski Most or military policemen?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These were military policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And policemen from Sanski Most guarded the compound. They were wearing proper police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you say "guarded the compound," what do you mean by "the compound"?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went behind the fence of the camp. They were behind the camp fence, because the camp had a wire fence and minefields. Barbed wire fence and mines were planted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, can I ask you next about, please, facilities. During the time you spent in Manjaca, which was until November of 1992, what were the arrangements about water?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation with water was very hard. We would get roughly 200 decilitres of water a day.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was there any water to wash or to -- wash yourself or wash clothes?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you ever during your period in Manjaca, were you ever able to have a shower?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What happened about shaving?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shaving was done by the detainees, but razors were missing, were in short supply so each detainee's turn would come once in eight or ten days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Food. At the beginning period in July, how much food were you getting?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning, when they were distributing food usually a loaf of 800 grammes would be cut up into 22 pieces and then each piece would be cut in half so that they would obtain 44 pieces out of that one loaf. And then for lunch, we would get the twenty-second part of an 800 gramme loaf, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you get any dinner, anything in the evening?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was there a change after you were registered by the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: After the Red Cross came in, was there adequate food and water?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 30th of August, yes. But again we didn't get water. We had to go and fetch water. When the Red Cross came, they brought us 5-litre cans, jerrycans. And if we went to fetch water for ourselves, then when we go to the lake, they would first order us to urinate and after that to fill the cans with water. I have to tell you once -- I have to tell you that on one occasion, I was glad because we were given orders to take that water to the command. They separated us into a line of ten men to take the water to the command.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So -- just so we understand, you were urinating into the water, which you then had to use for drinking water.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just while we're dealing with the Red Cross, I wonder if you can have a look at a photocopy, please, of your Red Cross card. You've got the original there. But if we can just have a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was one of the documents that was handed in at the later stage, that he brought with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Zulic, is that a photocopy of your Red Cross card?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you remember when you were registered?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly when. I believe it was the 17th of July. But right now I can't tell you exactly. I think it is written down in my diary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. You may be right, but we'll leave that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Your Honour, may that be made Prosecutor's Exhibit P826.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just to make sure, is it the document which has 5/3 at the top-right corner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As a matter of interest, that 5/3, Mr. Zulic -- you've got your original card there, I think. Who put that on?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was written by our commander, Muhamed Boskovic. He was in charge of facilitating talks between the command and the inmates.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And he also had to keep a record, a book of where the inmates were recorded. So this number means stable number 5, row number 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And on the back, are there some dates written? I think you need to have it back again. If you look at the second page of the photocopy, which is the back of the card, there seem to be some dates. Do you know what those are?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What's the first date?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This first date is the date when we were supposed to be released. I wrote that down because I didn't believe that we would be released on that day. And then it was moved to this other day. But as it turned out, we were released earlier. It turned out that I wasn't right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So those were the dates you expected to be released.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, you can take that now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Jumping ahead. As a result of the food and the like -- how much did you -- well, first of all, how much did you weigh roughly when you entered Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 90 kilogrammes or thereabout.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And how much did you weigh when you left, got to Karlovac?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, can I move to the question of interrogations. Were you and your fellow prisoners interrogated?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not, but others were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When they returned, others in your stable from interrogation, what sort of condition were they in?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually they were all beaten up. They had bruises on their backs, heads, legs, arms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Whilst you were in Manjaca, were you yourself beaten?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I was, but it wasn't as bad as they beat others. Once they beat me for saying that -- saying to the Red Cross that they could examine me. I allowed the Red Cross to examine me. And the other time they beat me because I walked on the grass -- I ate the grass.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: They beat you because you ate the grass?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They said, "Fuck you, balija, you're eating Serb grass -- you're grazing Serb grass."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then they hit me with their hands like this. They slapped me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It will sound like a silly question to you, Mr. Zulic, but why were you trying to eat grass -- or eating grass?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what else could I eat?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you say that the other time you were beaten, it was because you allowed the Red Cross to examine you.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time they beat me because of the Red Cross, and the second time because I ate grass.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you mean because the Red Cross carried out a medical examination of you, you were beaten up?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You say that you were not as badly beaten as some people. Did you witness other people being beaten?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I heard that other people would be taken out and beaten. Those people were Omer Filipovic, Esad Bender, from Trnava, Besic or -- or the other one. They told the Red Cross that it was all civilians that were imprisoned in Manjaca. And because of that statement, these two were unfortunately killed. We learned in the morning that they had been killed, whereas Besic managed to escape from the canal and today he lives in Trnava.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I should have asked you this: When you were examined by the Red Cross, did they find you had any injuries?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what injuries did you have?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My back was blue and black; my finger was broken, this one here -- this area here; and on my chest cage was all bruised; and I was the only one that agreed to be examined.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You told us about Omer Filipovic and Esad Bender. They were beaten because apparently they -- and died because they were -- spoke to the Red Cross. Did beatings take place on other occasions? Not maybe to you, but to other people that you knew.

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but both of those people died. Esad Bender and Omer Filipovic, both of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that, Mr. Zulic. But I want to talk about or ask you about other beatings. Were other people beaten? Not in connection to visits with the Red Cross but for other reasons?

utterances.speaker: AHMET ZULIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they were. Other people were beaten too. When they searched -- when they conducted a search, they found on Safet Mujagic a candle that he bought from Betonirka -- I'm sorry, not from Betonirka, from the hall.
